options: A catalogue listing every chart that Canada publishes
A chart of the approaches to the largest ports
The annual list of corrections to charts
The CHS key to chart symbols and terms
questions.explanation: Chart 1 is the key to the language of the chart. Its entries are grouped in lettered sections and each entry has a reference number. It is not a catalogue or a chart.

questions.stem: Which pairing of Chart 1 section letter and subject is correct?
options: I lights, K depths, P buoys and beacons, Q rocks and wrecks
I depths, K rocks/wrecks, P lights, Q buoys
H depths, K lights, P buoys and beacons, Q wrecks
B depths, I rocks, N lights, P buoys and beacons
questions.explanation: The four to remember are I (depths), K (rocks, wrecks, obstructions), P (lights) and Q (buoys and beacons). Section H is tides and currents, B is positions, distances, directions and compass, and N is areas and limits.

questions.stem: In which Chart 1 section would you look up the symbol for a prohibited anchorage area?
options: N, areas and limits
B, positions, distances, directions and compass
H, tides and currents
Q, buoys and beacons
questions.explanation: Anchorages and prohibited areas belong with areas and limits (section N). Section B covers compass roses and variation, and Q covers buoys and beacons.

questions.stem: A figure on a drying area of the chart is underlined: 2.4. What does it tell you?
options: There is 2.4 m of water at chart datum
A rock lies 2.4 m below the surface at high water
The seabed there stands 2.4 m above chart datum
The figure is a distance of 2.4 cables
questions.explanation: An underlined figure on a drying area is a drying height, an elevation above chart datum. A plain figure would be a depth below chart datum.

questions.stem: Part of a chart has no soundings at all and is marked as unsurveyed. How should you treat the water?
options: As deep water, because the surveyor found nothing to chart
As unknown, with possible dangers, and keep clear if you can
As shallow water, which is safe because you will feel the bottom
As open water that is safe at night but not by day
questions.explanation: An empty space on the chart is not evidence of deep water. Unsurveyed and inadequately surveyed areas carry a special symbol, and you treat them as unknown.

questions.stem: Which of these is a correct match of Chart 1 abbreviation and meaning?
options: Br breakers, M mud, S sand
Br bridge, M mud, S sand
Br breakers, M mud, S shingle
Br bottom rock, M mooring, S sand
questions.explanation: Br is breakers, M is mud and S is sand. Br is not a bridge and S is not shingle. Always look the less common letters up in Chart 1 instead of guessing.

questions.stem: A chart rose carries the note 2 degrees 45 minutes E 2008 (3 minutes W). What does the bracket tell you?
options: The easterly variation is increasing by 3 minutes each year
The deviation for the ship is 3 minutes west
The total variation is 3 minutes west
The easterly variation is decreasing by 3 minutes each year
questions.explanation: The bracket is the annual change, named by the direction it moves the variation. A westerly change makes easterly variation smaller. It says nothing about deviation, and it is a change per year, not the variation itself.

questions.stem: Draught 1.5 m, height of tide 0.3 m. Rock A covers and uncovers and is charted with (0.8) beside it. Rock B is an underwater rock of known depth, R 4.5. Rock C is awash at the level of chart datum. Which rocks have less than 1.5 m of water over them? (Invented figures.)
options: A and C
B only
A only
A, B and C
questions.explanation: Rock A's top is 0.8 m above chart datum and the tide is only 0.3 m, so the rock stands 0.5 m out of the water. Rock C is at datum, so it has 0.3 m over it. Rock B has 4.5 + 0.3 = 4.8 m over it, comfortably more than the draught. Rocks A and C are the ones that catch you at low tide.

questions.stem: A wreck is charted with an unknown least depth over it. How should it be treated?
options: As harmless, because no depth means deep water
As harmless once the tide is above chart datum
As dangerous to surface navigation
As dangerous only to vessels over 150 GT
questions.explanation: Without a known least depth you cannot say that your keel will clear it. Treat it as a danger. A wreck with a known safe depth is shown differently.

questions.stem: A sounding on a metric Canadian chart is printed as 9 with a small 4 beside it, lowered. What depth is it, and where is the position of the sounding?
options: 94 m, with the position at the foot of the figure
9.4 m, with the position at the centre of the figure
9.04 m, with the position at the centre of the figure
9 fathoms 4 feet, with the position at the left edge
questions.explanation: The small lowered figure is the decimetre part, so 9 and 4 is 9.4 m. The geographical position of a sounding is the centre of its figure. Soundings are in metres and decimetres to 21 m and whole metres beyond.

questions.stem: You want to anchor and the chart shows an area where anchoring is prohibited. What is the correct view of that symbol?
options: A restriction to obey, not a suggestion
It is advice only and may be ignored in fine weather
It applies only to vessels over 15 GT
It applies only at night
questions.explanation: Prohibited-area symbols show where entry, anchoring, fishing or diving is not permitted. Find another anchorage.
